title: CoolingPath
description:
One coolant route from a source to the thing it cools, following the NetBox/Nautobot 4.7 liquid-cooling model: CoolingSource to CoolingFeed to CoolingIntake and CoolingOutflow. Adopting their shape rather than inventing one means the crosswalk is field-for-field, and it is the reason this contract needs no RDF -- the IT/OT requirement turned out to be expressible in a flat relational form.

This entity is why converged observability is possible at all. A GPU throttling at the top of a rack and a CDU running at reduced flow are the same incident, and nothing in a GPU-centric data model can connect them. The path is the connection: it names the source, the feed, and every resource downstream, so a flow deficit at the source has a computable blast radius.

Coolant *ports* are Port records with `port_class: coolant`, and the physical hoses between them are Links. This entity is the route through them, not a replacement for them.

name.description: Path name as the facility uses it, typically naming the CDU and the loop: `CDU-01 secondary loop A`.

source_resource_id.description: Where the coolant comes from: a CDU, or a facility connection for a primary loop. NetBox's CoolingSource.

loop.description: Which loop this path belongs to. The distinction matters because the primary and secondary loops are separated by a heat exchanger and owned by different organizations -- facilities owns one, the deployment team owns the other -- and a fault on either side presents identically at the rack.

feed_resource_ids.description: The distribution chain in flow order, source-side first: manifolds, busbar-mounted hoses, quick disconnects. NetBox's CoolingFeed. Order matters, because an isolation valve halfway along determines what a shutdown affects.

intake_port_id.description: Coolant inlet port on the cooled resource. NetBox's CoolingIntake, expressed as a Port here so intake and outflow sit in the same topology graph as every other termination point.

cooled_resource_ids.description: Everything this path removes heat from. Denormalized on purpose, and the one place in this contract where that is the right call: it is the blast radius of a cooling fault, it is read on every alert, and deriving it means walking the feed chain and the containment tree on each read.

design.description: Commissioned design point. This is the `expected` side of a cooling validation, and the numbers a measured reading is compared against.

delta_p_kpa.description: Design pressure drop across the path. A measured drop above design is the signature of a partial blockage, which is otherwise invisible until something throttles.

heat_capacity_kw.description: Heat this path is rated to remove. Compared against the summed thermal_design_watts of `cooled_resource_ids` -- if the sum exceeds this, the rack cannot run at full load and the failure will look like random throttling.

redundancy.description: Redundancy tier of the SOURCE serving this path. Recorded because it is the difference between a CDU pump failure being a maintenance ticket and being a rack-down event, and that is a design decision worth being able to audit after the fact.
